_readme: Raw materials master data for Stumarcot, transcribed from the user's 'Materials master.md' project doc (2026-10-12). Purchase unit = what the supplier sells in. Inventory unit = what MOIS tracks stock in. conversion_to_inventory_unit = how many inventory units per 1 purchase unit. qty_on_hand and last_recorded_price are intentionally null here - this file defines the material catalog, not current stock or cost; those are live, user-entered, transaction-derived values per the user's own note ('qty is the stock count and cost is the current price as last recorded by user') and belong in the database (1b materials ledger), not a static seed value that goes stale. IMPORTANT (added 2026-10-12): every material's 'source' field and every price figure in this file is DODOMA BRANCH data only. Mwanza and Dar es Salaam may buy the same materials from different suppliers at different prices - confirmed by the user. The production/consumption FLOW is the same across all three branches (same recipes, same ratios, same conversions) - only sourcing and purchase price vary by branch. This is structurally identical to how product pricing already varies by branch (product_branch_pricing) - materials need the same per-branch treatment, not a single global 'source' text field on the material.

_decisions_log.decision: Transcribed verbatim from 'Materials master.md'. No quantities or prices were given in the source - left null, not guessed.
_decisions_log.action_taken: Created this file as the seed input for 1a.1's materials master data and 1b's materials ledger.

_decisions_log.topic: Open: which sand type per recipe
_decisions_log.decision: Three distinct sand materials exist (Mchanga Laini, Mweupe, Mnene) from two sources, but every recipe in ratios_and_molds.json specifies generic 'mchanga' with no type. NOT guessed - recipes keep generic 'mchanga' as the material reference until the user specifies which sand type each product category actually uses. RESOLVED 2026-10-12: see per-material notes and ratios_and_molds.json for the full category/item mapping.
_decisions_log.action_taken: Flagged as open. material_id 'mchanga_generic' kept as a placeholder reference in recipes until resolved; the 3 specific sand materials exist in this file as real purchasable/stockable materials regardless. Mapping applied: vibro categories -> Mweupe; press paving + Chipping/Hollow Block + Kerbstones + Culverts + Posts&Bicons -> Laini; plain Sand Block/Tofali only -> Mnene.

_decisions_log.decision: Not an ingredient in any recipe in ratios_and_molds.json. Likely machine fuel or lubricant (operational cost), not a BOM material. Not assumed either way.
_decisions_log.action_taken: Included as a material (it's a real purchased, stocked item) but flagged as not yet linked to any recipe or cost category - needs user confirmation of its purpose before 1d (production costing) decides whether it's a per-unit production cost or a fixed overhead.

_decisions_log.topic: Source/price is per-branch, not global - correction to earlier default
_decisions_log.decision: User confirmed: all material data gathered so far is Dodoma-specific. Mwanza and Dar es Salaam may source the same materials from different suppliers at different prices. The production flow (recipes, ratios, conversions) is identical across branches - only sourcing/price varies. This corrects the earlier default (a single plain-text 'source' field on the material) - source and purchase price need a per-branch structure, mirroring product_branch_pricing exactly, not a single column.
_decisions_log.action_taken: Tagged every material's existing source as Dodoma-specific in this file. Schema correction relayed to Claude Code before the materials foundation work is built, so it isn't built against the wrong (single global source) assumption.

materials.note: Used in: press-machine paving (Rectangular/Zigzag/H-Paver/Worldcup/Z-Plain/W-Cup), the Chipping and Hollow Block items in Blocks (NOT the plain Sand Block/Tofali items - those use Mchanga Mnene), Kerbstones (50/80 Press), Culverts, and Posts & Bicons (Nguzo/Bicon).
